video_title: Major Drama Coming From The Jazz At The Draft?

quotes.speaker: Tim McMahon
quotes.summary_phrase: Utah Jazz are undecided on their number two overall pick
quotes.excerpt: I don't believe they know which guy they're picking.
quotes.quote: There are three alternatives and I don't believe the Jazz know who is going to be there. Number one, they don't know who is going to be there, who is going number one. Number two, whoever is there at two, I don't believe they know which guy they're picking. Now, if it's AJ Dybantsa, if it's Darren Peterson, if it's Cameron Boozer, I think all those three guys are in play for the Jazz at this point.

quotes.speaker: Tim McMahon
quotes.summary_phrase: Jazz lack a clear-cut face of the franchise player
quotes.excerpt: They still don't have a clear-cut face of the franchise.
quotes.quote: The Jazz have done a lot of things over the last few years to build up their roster to put themselves in a chance to be competitive this year, to compete for a postseason spot. They still don't have a clear-cut face of the franchise. Jaren Jackson Jr. is a very good player, not a face of a franchise. Same with Lauri Markkanen. Keyonte George took a major leap last year, not a face of the franchise. Ace Bailey has the potential to maybe be that guy, but no sure thing. They've got to pick a guy at two who has a chance to develop into that sort of a player.

quotes.speaker: Tim McMahon
quotes.summary_phrase: Cameron Boozer's rebounding makes him a strong fit for Utah
quotes.excerpt: Jaren Jackson Jr. is a poor rebounder for a five. Well, Boozer would really mitigate that concern.
quotes.quote: Part of the evaluation is Jaren Jackson Jr.'s flaw playing the five, and I'm not saying he'd start there, but playing there, he's a poor rebounder for a five. Well, Boozer would really mitigate that concern because he's a really strong rebounder for a four, right? And Boozer as a four, part of the concern is you really need a rim protector alongside him. Obviously Jaren Jackson Jr. is an elite rim protector, so those guys would, you could see them as a great complementary duo.

quotes.speaker: Tim McMahon
quotes.summary_phrase: Utah Jazz are looking to negotiate a contract extension with Keyonte George
quotes.excerpt: The Jazz think those two guys could fit very well.
quotes.quote: There is one more thing I want to mention about the Darren Peterson-Utah dynamic. He's represented by the same agency that represents Keyonte George. My understanding is the Jazz think those two guys could fit very well. Keyonte is kind of a 1.5, Peterson is kind of a 1.5. Peterson is probably more of a two than a one. Keyonte had a breakout year last year. I'm not sure the agency feels as strongly about their fit, but I think the agency's opinion might be influenced by the unlikelihood of Keyonte George getting a contract extension this summer.

quotes.speaker: Tim McMahon
quotes.summary_phrase: Utah Jazz are facing a tense restricted free agency situation
quotes.excerpt: This has a chance to be a very tense restricted free agency situation.
quotes.quote: The Jazz want to be good. That means they're going to have to negotiate hard. They're obviously not going to be a free agency destination. They're becoming very expensive. The trade for Jaren Jackson Jr. really vaulted them from a payroll perspective. Just like they've been negotiating hard with Darren Peterson, I think they're going to take the same approach with Keyonte George. This has a chance to be a very tense restricted free agency situation.
